instructions: Cut the tomatoes in half. Grate the cut sides on the big holes of a box grater into a colander set over a bowl, until only the skins are left, and throw the skins away. Leave the tomato to drain for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, crumble the feta into a bowl with a fork. Pit the olives and cut them in half.

Set the rusks on four plates. Sprinkle each with 4 tbsp water and drizzle each with 1 tbsp of the oil. Leave them for 2 minutes. They should give a little when you press them but still be firm in the middle.
Spoon the drained tomato over the rusks and add a pinch of salt and pepper.
Top with the feta, olives and capers, then sprinkle with the oregano. Drizzle each with another 1 tbsp of the oil. Serve right away.
method_notes: My Greek Dish leads (rusk moistened with water and oil, drained grated tomato, crumbled cheese, olives and capers). It tops the dakos with feta and myzithra; this uses feta alone (7 oz) so there is one cheese to buy. The Hungry Bites uses a quick dip in water instead of sprinkling, and the same tomato and feta. The barley rusks are not gluten-free.
